newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Abidjan port paralysed by dockers strike.
newsitem.headline: Abidjan port paralysed by dockers strike.

text.p: Work was paralysed at Abidjan port on Tuesday following an indefinite pay strike by dock workers, strikers and witnesses said.

Strike leaders said the action started on Monday and would continue until the pay dispute was resolved. There was no sign of loading or other activity at the port but no official assessment of the effect of the stoppage was available.
The port of San Pedro to the west, which like Abidjan handles Ivory Coast's cocoa exports, was not affected.
"We have no fixed salaries, we are paid by the hour and we have been working in this condition for years," declared Zadi Nadje Daniel, a spokesman for the dockers.
"What we want now is fixed salaries plus annual bonuses as exists in other sectors," he told reporters, adding, "We are not going back to work until our demands are met."
The action continued on Tuesday despite a meeting between the Abidjan Ports Authority management and union leaders on Monday night.

No comment was immediately available from management with most businesses in Abidjan shut early for Christmas. Dockers said, however, their leaders were continuing round-the-clock talks with management.
